extracted.intended_audience: Federal agency NEPA practitioners, environmental compliance officers, agency counsel, and consultants preparing or reviewing EISs/EAs and agency NEPA procedures
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory requirements for Federal agencies on how to implement NEPA procedurally and how to prepare concise, informative, and efficient environmental documents (EISs, EAs), including scoping, tiering, and related processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonably foreseeable
rubrics_metrics.description: Application of 'reasonably foreseeable' is influenced by the context of the proposed action; agencies are not required to 'foresee the unforeseeable' or engage in speculative analysis; agencies must forecast to the extent they can either quantitatively or qualitatively within a reasonable range; the term is consistent with the ordinary person standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An ordinary person standard applies—what a person of ordinary prudence would consider. CEQ notes no practical challenges from this connection and warns that changing the regulatory text could create unnecessary uncertainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope (§1508.1(kk))
rubrics_metrics.description: The definition of 'scope' includes EAs and covers both the range and breadth of the actions, alternatives, and effects to be considered in an EIS or EA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scope is a fact-specific analysis informed by an agency's statutory authority and control/responsibility over the activity; CEQ revised the definition to include EAs and removed non-definitional tiering language (addressed elsewhere).

rubrics_metrics.name: Significant effects (§1508.1(mm))
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Significant effects' are adverse effects identified by an agency as significant based on the criteria set forth in §1501.3(d); beneficial effects are not 'significant effects' for purposes of requiring an EIS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ's approach means an agency does not need to prepare an EIS if a proposed action's effects are exclusively beneficial, but agencies must still analyze both adverse and beneficial effects in NEPA documents if they are reasonably foreseeable. CEQ considered comments for and against limiting 'significant effects' to adverse effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tiering (§1508.1(oo))
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition revised to cross-reference the tiering process set forth in §1501.11.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revision avoids inconsistency between a definitional provision and the substantive tiering provisions in §1501.11; comments on application of tiering are addressed in other sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose (§1500.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: NEPA is the basic national charter for protection of the environment; it establishes policy, sets goals, and provides direction for carrying out the policy (citing section 101(a) and 101(b) purposes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulations in this subchapter implement NEPA and ensure agencies identify, consider, and disclose relevant environmental information early in the process. The President, Federal agencies, and courts share responsibility for enforcing the Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpret and administer policies consistent with NEPA (§1500.2(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal agencies shall interpret and administer the policies, regulations, and public laws of the United States in accordance with the policies set forth in NEPA and these regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make NEPA process useful; reduce paperwork; emphasize important issues (§1500.2(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies shall implement procedures to make NEPA more useful to decision makers and the public; reduce paperwork and extraneous background data; and emphasize important environmental issues and alternatives. Environmental documents shall be concise, clear, and supported by evidence that agencies have conducted necessary analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on issues truly relevant to the action rather than amassing needless detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate NEPA with other planning and review procedures (§1500.2(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Integrate NEPA requirements with other planning and environmental review procedures required by law or agency practice so such procedures run concurrently rather than consecutively where doing so promotes efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage and facilitate public engagement (§1500.2(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies shall encourage and facilitate public engagement in decisions that affect the human environment, including meaningful engagement with communities such as those with environmental justice concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use NEPA to identify reasonable alternatives to avoid/minimize adverse effects (§1500.2(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the NEPA process to identify and assess reasonable alternatives that will avoid or minimize adverse effects, including alternatives that reduce climate change-related effects or address disproportionate impacts on environmental justice communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use practicable means to restore/enhance and avoid/minimize adverse effects (§1500.2(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Use all practicable means, consistent with the Act and other considerations of national policy, to restore and enhance the quality of the human environment and avoid or minimize any possible adverse effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: NEPA compliance - mandate and applicability (§1500.3(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: This subchapter is applicable to and binding on all Federal agencies for implementing NEPA's procedural provisions; the regulations implement section 102(2) and must be read with the Act as a whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issued pursuant to NEPA and other statutes and EOs cited in the authority statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of NEPA compliance (§1500.3(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Council's intention that judicial review of agency compliance should not occur before an agency issues the record of decision or other final agency action (with limited exceptions); minor non-substantive errors that have no effect on decisionmaking are harmless and shall not invalidate an agency action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allegations of noncompliance should be resolved expeditiously as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Severability (§1500.3(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections of the subchapter are separate and severable; if a section is stayed or held invalid, validity of remaining parts should not be affected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meeting appropriate page limits (§1500.4(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies shall prepare analytical, concise, and informative environmental documents by meeting appropriate page limits (see §§1501.5(g) and 1502.7).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page limits are intended to promote concision and focus on important issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discuss only briefly issues other than important ones (§1500.4(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Environmental documents should discuss non-important issues only briefly (e.g., see §1502.2(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concentrate on issues truly relevant to the action rather than amassing needless detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write environmental documents in plain language (§1500.4(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Environmental documents shall be written in plain language (see §1502.8).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plain language aids public understanding and usefulness to decisionmakers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow a clear format for environmental impact statements (§1500.4(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies shall follow a clear format for EISs (see §1502.10).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistent clear formats help readers find key information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasize portions most useful to decisionmakers and public (§1500.4(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Emphasize portions of documents that are most useful to decisionmakers and the public and reduce emphasis on background material (see §§1502.14, 1502.15, 1502.16 and §1502.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize information that informs decisions and public input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use scoping to identify and narrow important issues (§1500.4(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the scoping process to identify important environmental issues deserving study and to deemphasize unimportant issues, narrowing the scope of the EIS (or EA where elected) (§§1501.9 and 1502.4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scoping helps focus analyses on key issues and avoids unnecessary analysis of marginal issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summarize the environmental impact statement (§1500.4(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies shall provide a concise summary of the EIS (§1502.12).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A clear summary increases accessibility for decisionmakers and the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use programmatic documents and tiering to avoid repetition (§1500.4(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: Use programmatic environmental documents and tiering from broad to narrower documents to eliminate repetitive discussions (§1501.11).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tiering and programmatic analyses can streamline subsequent project-level review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporate by reference where appropriate (§1500.4(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporate materials by reference as authorized (§1501.12) to avoid duplicative content in the body of documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporation by reference reduces document length while making necessary materials available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate NEPA with other review and consultation requirements (§1500.4(j))
rubrics_metrics.description: Integrate NEPA requirements with other environmental review and consultation requirements (see §1502.24).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concurrent integration promotes efficiency and avoids duplication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require comments be as specific as possible (§1500.4(k))
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments on environmental documents must be as specific as possible (§1503.3) to be fully considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specificity enables agencies to respond meaningfully and address concerns in analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: When changes are minor, publish only the changes to the draft EIS (§1500.4(l))
rubrics_metrics.description: When changes are minor, agencies should attach and publish only changes to the draft EIS rather than rewriting and publishing the entire statement (§1503.4(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This avoids unnecessary republication of largely unchanged documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eliminate duplication with State, Tribal, and local procedures; joint preparation and adoption (§1500.4(m))
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should eliminate duplication with State, Tribal, and local procedures by providing for joint preparation of environmental documents where practicable (§1506.2), and may adopt appropriate documents prepared by another Federal agency (§1506.3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Joint preparation and adoption promote efficiency and reduce burdens on stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combine environmental documents with other documents (§1500.4(n))
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies may combine environmental documents with other documents where appropriate (§1506.4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combining documents can reduce duplication and streamline review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish categorical exclusions (§1500.5(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies shall establish categorical exclusions defining categories of actions that normally do not have a significant effect on the human environment and therefore do not require preparation of an EA or EIS (§§1501.4 and 1507.3(c)(8)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Categorical exclusions promote efficiency by removing routine actions from EA/EIS requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use a finding of no significant impact (FONSI) when appropriate (§1500.5(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a FONSI when an action not otherwise excluded will not have a significant effect on the human environment and therefore does not require an EIS (§1501.6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FONSIs allow efficient resolution for actions without significant impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate NEPA into early planning (§1500.5(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Integrate the NEPA process into early planning (§1501.2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early integration reduces delays and improves decisionmaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage in interagency cooperation early (§1500.5(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage in interagency cooperation, including with affected Federal, State, Tribal, and local agencies, before or during preparation of an EA or EIS rather than waiting to request/submit comments on a completed document (§§1501.7 and 1501.8).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early cooperation promotes coordinated, consistent, and timely reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure swift and fair resolution of lead agency disputes (§1500.5(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies shall ensure the swift and fair resolution of lead agency disputes (§1501.7).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prompt resolution of lead agency disputes supports timely NEPA processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use scoping for early identification of important issues (§1500.5(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the scoping process to identify important issues that require detailed analysis (§1502.4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scoping narrows analyses to significant issues and promotes efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meet appropriate deadlines for EA and EIS processes (§1500.5(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies shall meet appropriate deadlines for the environmental assessment and environmental impact statement processes (§1501.10).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely adherence to schedules reduces delays and uncertainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare environmental documents early in the process (§1500.5(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare environmental documents early in the process (§§1502.5 and 1501.5(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early preparation ensures environmental considerations inform decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate NEPA with other review and consultation requirements (repeated) (§1500.5(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Integrate NEPA requirements with other environmental review and consultation requirements (§1502.24).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reiterates integration to promote concurrent reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eliminate duplication with State, Tribal, and local procedures; joint prep or adoption (§1500.5(j))
rubrics_metrics.description: Eliminate duplication by providing for joint preparation of environmental documents where practicable (§1506.2) and by allowing agencies to jointly prepare or adopt appropriate documents prepared by another agency (§1506.3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Joint preparation/adoption reduces duplicative effort across governments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combine environmental documents with other documents (repeated) (§1500.5(k))
rubrics_metrics.description: Combine environmental documents with other documents where appropriate (§1506.4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeated emphasis on combining documents to increase efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use accelerated procedures for legislative proposals (§1500.5(l))
rubrics_metrics.description: Use accelerated procedures for proposals for legislation (§1506.8).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special procedures can expedite NEPA considerations for legislative proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency authority (§1500.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall interpret the Act's provisions as a supplement to existing authority and as a mandate to view policies and missions in light of NEPA's objectives; agencies shall review and revise policies, procedures, and regulations as necessary to ensure compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The phrase 'to the fullest extent possible' means each agency shall comply with NEPA unless exempted by law or compliance is impossible.
